paper_summary: Salleh et al. synthesised vinyl ester / glass microballoon syntactic foams (Potters Q-CEL 5020 borosilicate hollow microspheres, 72 um mean size, 110 kg/m3 bulk density) at 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 wt% by stir mixing and open-mould casting, and characterised density, porosity/void content, tensile (ASTM D638) and compressive (ASTM D695) behaviour plus SEM fractography. Density falls linearly with microballoon content while both tensile and compressive strength and moduli fall below neat vinyl ester; SCFT-01 (2 wt%) gives the best specific tensile and specific compressive properties. Tensile moduli are reported to be 70-80% higher than compressive moduli, attributed to particle-matrix debonding and to microballoon fracture within the 40-90 MPa range used for the compressive modulus fit.

extraction_notes: MAJOR LIMITATION: Table 1 - the paper's single data table, which holds the per-specimen density, wall thickness, radius ratio, cavity/matrix porosity, void content and the tensile and compressive strength/modulus values with CoVs - is NOT present in the extracted text. Figures 4, 7, 8 and 13 (density, stress-strain curves, strength/modulus vs wt%, relative modulus) are also images only. Consequently only the four numeric property values quoted in the running text could be captured: neat vinyl ester tensile strength 39 MPa, neat vinyl ester compressive strength 112 MPa, SCFT-01 compressive strength 89 MPa with specific compressive strength 86 MPa/(g/cm3), and SCFT-02 tensile modulus 9.92 GPa (recorded as 9920 MPa). The 9.92 GPa figure is physically implausible for a vinyl ester syntactic foam (neat vinyl ester is typically ~3-3.5 GPa) and the paper's own statement that tensile modulus is 70-80% above compressive modulus is not consistent with any other reported number; it is recorded verbatim as printed with low extractor_confidence and should be treated as suspect. Remaining composition x test cells are kept as records with null properties so the experimental matrix is preserved. Unit conversions: GPa x 1000 -> MPa; wt% and vol% -> fractions (0-1); particle bulk density 110 kg/m3 -> 0.11 g/cm3 (the paper calls this 'bulk density' from the manufacturer data sheet but uses it as the microballoon density throughout, and elsewhere quotes 190 kg/m3 from the missing Table 1). Volume fractions are stated only for SCFT-01 (4 vol%) and SCFT-05 (8 vol%); the rest are left null rather than interpolated. Porosity values in the text are mutually inconsistent (SCFT-01 cavity 57% / matrix 16%, versus 'on average 12% contain both porosities', versus void content 2.7-3.8%, versus 'increased from 33% to 53%'), so no numeric matrix_porosity_fraction was entered; the figures are recorded in microstructure_notes instead. Curing was 24 h at room temperature followed by 4 h post-cure at 60-80 C; no single cure temperature is stated so cure_or_process_temperature_c is left null. Test temperature set to 25 C (ambient; the paper states the pycnometry was done at 25 C but does not state a mechanical test temperature). Strain rates left null: only crosshead speeds are given (1.25 mm/min tension, 2 mm/min compression), and the tensile gauge length is ambiguous (25 mm extensometer on an ASTM D638 dog bone). Comparison data for other vinyl ester syntactic foams (Fig. 14/15, from ref [17] Gupta et al.) are plotted only, with no readable numbers, so no secondary records were created.
